abstract:
Abstract
Early and accurate detection of brain tumors in MRI images is important for increasing patient survival rates. The latest trends in Deep Learning (DL) have revolutionized medical imaging analysis. This paper presents a systematic review of state-of-the-art methodologies, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Transformers, Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), and Explainable AI (XAI). It also summarizes the information on pre-processing techniques, commonly available datasets, and evaluation metrics. Following that, experimental validation is performed on various DL models, including CNNs, a Custom Deep CNN (for Ablation), transfer learning models (VGG16, ResNet50, EfficientNetB0), and a Swin Transformer. The transformer achieved the superior Mean ± Std accuracy (0.97 ± 0.02), Precision 99%, Recall 99% and F1-score (98%) across 5 Runs. Moreover, the Attention Maps of the Swin Transformer are evaluated, providing insight into the decision-making process of DL models. Finally, the study also highlights existing challenges and outlines future research directions, including federated learning, self-supervised approaches, and lightweight hybrid architectures to build scalable, interpretable diagnostic models.

  - heading "Introduction" [level=2]
  - generic: Irregular cell growth within the delicate structure of the brain increases the risk of a brain tumor that can be malignant or benign [1]. It reduces the oxygen and nutrient supply to the human body, disturbing normal functions and destroying healthy cells [2]. As shown in Fig. 1, tumors can be identified as regions of the brain that deviate in intensity from healthy brain tissue. In the US alone, more than 88,000 adults and 5500 children are diagnosed with brain tumors [3].
  - generic: The prognosis for brain tumor patients sharply decreases with age. For example, the five-year survival rate decreases from approximately 74% in children to 21% in adults over 40 years old [4]. Significantly, to support the brain tumor community and to raise awareness of this life-threatening disease, World Brain Tumor Day is celebrated on 8th June every year. Detecting, classifying, and assessing the brain tumor at an early stage is required to overcome the severe consequences [5].
  - generic: To this end, several methods, such as surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy, targeted therapies, and immunotherapy, are used for treatment purposes [6]. The treatment of the patient also depends on various factors, including the age of the patient, the type of tumor, the size of the tumor, and the location of the tumor [7].
  - generic: Several methods are usually used, such as MRI, X-ray, CT, Biopsy, and PET, to examine the tumor tissues [7]. The traditional method of biopsy is effective but painful and time-consuming. Also, manual analysis of medical images is a time-consuming task that demands the efforts of radiologists and could result in incorrect diagnosis because of its complexity [9]. To overcome these issues, medical images are processed to extract handcrafted features and to train and test the classifier, including Support Vector Machine, k-nearest neighbors, and Decision Tree. These conventional approaches to extracting features of MRI images are time-consuming and subject to error, which greatly diminishes accuracy [10]. To address these challenges, DL-pretrained models such as VGG16, ResNet, and EfficientNet have been instrumental for automatic feature extraction. In addition, transformer and GNN architectures are employed to learn spatial relationships among tumor pixels [11]. Moreover, Hybrid methods are becoming increasingly popular for creating stronger, more trustworthy AI systems. The implementation of Explainable AI methods in AI models assists medical practitioners in analyzing the tumor classification predictions [12].

  - generic: "This paper is structured as follows: Section 1 introduces the motivation and contributions. Background clinical information regarding brain tumors and medical imaging is mentioned in Section 2. Section 3 analyzes image preprocessing techniques, while Section 4 reviews deep learning models for classification. Additionally, publicly available datasets and benchmarks for brain tumor diagnosis are explored in Section 5, and Section 6 depicts the experimental validation of some DL models. Lastly, 7 Results, 8 Research challenges and gaps discuss challenges and future directions, respectively, and Section 9 presents the conclusion."
